headline: Best week of the block on paper, but volume and pace both ran well ahead of the plan while HRV/RHR baselines drifted the wrong way all week — hold the plan and hit it as written, not more.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 9 August 2026

**Week of 3–9 August. Week 3 of the Cheltenham build. 42 days to race day.**

## How the week actually went

| | This week | Last week | Week before |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volume | **73.7 km** | 62.5 km | 47.5 km |
| Runs | 6 | 8 | 6 |
| Elevation | 384 m | 591 m | 269 m |
| Quality time | 159 min | 53 min | 33 min |
| Easy share | 55% | 82% | 86% |
| Efficiency | **1.498** | 1.471 | 1.426 |
| Avg HRV | 36.4 | 43.9 | 40.0 |
| Avg RHR | 48.6 | 46.7 | — |

Both quality sessions landed, achilles read zero on every running day, and
efficiency hit a new high for the block. On the surface this looks like the
best week yet. It's also the week that needs the most scrutiny, because two
things happened that the plan didn't ask for.

**The plan called for ~61 km this week** (rest, 8, 8, 8, 7, 12, 18). You ran
**73.7 km** — 12.7 km over, and above even the 68 km ceiling I set deliberately
last review ("the return on 75 km is negative"). The overshoot isn't spread
evenly — it's concentrated in the two hard days:

- **Wed 5 Aug (intervals):** planned 6–8 km total, logged **14.0 km**. Note:
  "We had wind! 12mph."
- **Sat 8 Aug (tempo):** planned 12 km (4x10min threshold or 25–30min
  continuous), but logged as **session_type "intervals"**, **18.3 km**, RPE 7.
  Note: "reps 1&2 seemed tough but 3 OK and 4 too but I'd say I felt more
  flat footed on the 4th." Four reps described doesn't match either the
  planned Saturday tempo format or the standard Wednesday interval format —
  worth a word from you on what actually got run Saturday, because right now
  the log and the plan disagree on both distance and session type.
- **Today's long run:** hit the 18 km target on distance, but at 4:29/km
  average (HR 150) — quicker than the prescribed long-run zone
  (4:36–4:59/km) and quicker than any long run this block bar the two
  quality-tagged ones. In 28.4°C heat.

None of these individually is alarming. Together, the pattern this week is
"faster and longer than written" on three separate days, not one.

## How he's coping — data and his own words

Every day this week reads "good" or "caution" in isolation — nothing hit
"flag" with a session attached. But look at the trend across the seven days
rather than any single reading, per the brief's own rule:

| | 3 Aug | 4 Aug | 5 Aug | 6 Aug | 7 Aug | 8 Aug | 9 Aug |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HRV baseline (7d) | 43.9 | 42.7 | 39.7 | 39.0 | 38.7 | 36.7 | 36.3 |
| RHR baseline (7d) | 46.7 | 46.7 | 47.6 | 47.7 | 48.0 | 48.6 | 48.7 |
| ACWR | 1.0 | 0.9 | 1.1 | 1.1 | 1.1 | 1.3 | 1.4 |

A steady, one-directional slide: HRV baseline down ~17% across the week, RHR
baseline up, ACWR climbing to 1.4 by Sunday. Sleep is still genuinely good
(86–90 score, 7.7–8.9 hrs) so this doesn't read as exhaustion — but it's
exactly the shape of drift you'd expect from a week that ran ~20% over its
planned volume, with two sessions run further and faster than written, in a
week with **four "high" heat-risk days** (31.1°C, 26.4°C, 26.5°C, 28.4°C).

His own notes this week were upbeat and matter-of-fact throughout — "all
good," "felt easy," nothing alarming in tone. That's worth taking at face
value; he's not describing a bad week. But the data trend and the subjective
read can both be true at once: he feels fine *and* the numbers are drifting
in a direction that, left unchecked, is how an achilles or a heat problem
starts.

## Achilles

Scored 0 on every running day this week (1 on the Monday rest day, resolved
immediately). No cause for concern in the numbers. The one thing to log
mentally: "more flat footed on the 4th" rep on Saturday. Score was 0, but
that's a subjective, gait-related comment in the exact watch-item this brief
flags — not a red flag on its own, but worth asking about specifically next
week rather than letting it pass as incidental colour.

## Efficiency trend

Still climbing: 1.418 → 1.456 → 1.426 → 1.471 → **1.498**. Genuinely good
news, and it held up through the highest-volume, hottest week of the build
so far.

## Race countdown

42 days to Cheltenham (6.0 weeks). Prediction: **1:22:23** (range
1:20:09–1:24:37), unchanged and consistent with the brief's estimate.
Remaining key sessions: 4 tempo, 5 intervals, 4 long. Longest run in the
last four weeks is now effectively today's 18 km (~81 min); next week's
planned 20 km clears the 95-minute pre-taper target on schedule.

## Recommendation: **hold**

Next week's plan (already approved, from the 2 Aug proposal) is: rest,
easy 8, intervals 9, easy 8, easy 6, tempo 13, long 20. That's the right
progression — accelerating the long run toward the pre-taper target exactly
as planned. I'm not adding anything to it.

But "hold the plan" this week means something specific: **run the sessions
as written, not a bit more.** This week's actual training already outran the
plan on its own — longer intervals, a tempo that turned into something else
entirely, and a long run at quicker-than-prescribed pace — and the HRV/RHR
trend across the week is the kind of quiet signal that shows up before a
bigger one does. He's 42 days out with an achilles history and a heat
sensitivity; there's no version of this build where banking extra,
faster kilometres now is worth more than staying sharp and uninjured in
September. Next week's 20 km long run and 13 km tempo are enough of a step
up on their own — no need to add to them.

One thing worth a direct question rather than a guess: what actually
happened on Saturday. If it was a genuine session swap (intervals instead
of tempo) that's fine to know about; if it's a logging mismatch, good to fix
before it muddies next week's comparison too.
